items.title: City of Edmonton, 2023-2026 Capital Budget (adopted December 2022), Appendix A and capital profile CM-20-0330

citations.finding: Capital profile CM-20-0330 'Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3' is listed in Appendix A (in $000s) at 5,950 (2023), 26,750 (2024), 33,650 (2025), 33,650 (2026), total 100,000, status Approved, page 103; the profile sheet (pages 540-543) shows the same cash flow, funding source Tax-Supported Debt, profile type Composite, Service Category blank.
citations.establishes: The approved amount, years and per-year allocation of the $100 million program.
citations.quote: CM-20-0330 Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 5,950 26,750 33,650 33,650 100,000 - Approved

citations.finding: Appendix A 'List of Capital Profiles by Asset Category ($000's)', pages 101-105, gives the 2023-2026 approved amount for each profile; summing the 18 Service Category 'Roads' profiles (excluding 21-20-2100 and 14-66-2570), the 11 'Neighbourhood Renewal' profiles and the three bridge profiles gives 1,945,703 ($000s). The 'Service Category' field on each profile sheet (pages 376-670) was read for all 161 sheets; 20 read 'Roads', 11 read 'Neighbourhood Renewal', and 23-24-0300, 21-24-9301, 21-24-9302 and CM-20-0330 are blank.
citations.establishes: The roads-only approved total under the primary boundary: $1,945.7 million, 19.5 times $100 million.
citations.quote: CM-99-9600 Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion: Project Delivery 17,200 133,027 137,012 89,016 376,255 24,158 Previously Approved

citations.finding: Table 8 'Adopted Capital Budget by Service' (page 56, $ millions): under 'Movement of People and Goods', 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' 2023-2026 Growth 622.8, Renewal 1,171.2, Total 1,794.0; 2027 and beyond 108.6; overall total 1,902.6. 'Transit Service' 446.5; 'Total Movement of People and Goods' 2,256.0. Under 'Transforming for the Future': LRT Expansion 2,374.9; Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion 493.4. The document describes the total as the approved $7.91 billion 2023-2026 Capital Budget.
citations.establishes: The required alternative: the combined 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' allocation of $1,794.0 million (17.9 times $100 million), which is the published figure closest to the councillor's $1.8 billion; it includes active pathways and is not a roads total.

citations.finding: Profiles labelled 'Roads' on their sheets include the four Yellowhead Trail profiles (493,400 combined) that Table 8 reports as the transformational 'Yellowhead Trail Freeway Conversion' project rather than under 'Active Pathways and Roads Service'; without them the primary total is 1,452,303 ($000s), 14.5 times, which would be Partially supported. The 'Roads'-only narrowest reading is 1,116,532, 11.2 times.
citations.establishes: That the roads total depends on where the boundary is drawn; the councillor's figure holds on the primary and on Table 8's combined line but not on the narrowest reading.

citations.finding: The 2023-2026 capital budget approved $100 million for Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 (CM-20-0330).
citations.establishes: The total approved capital funding for the active transportation program.

citations.finding: The sum of 2023-2026 capital profiles for Service Category 'Roads', 'Neighbourhood Renewal', and three specified bridges equals $1,945.7 million.
citations.establishes: The total approved capital funding for roads under the primary boundary.

citations.finding: Table 8 'Adopted Capital Budget by Service' includes a combined line for 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' of $1,794.0 million.
citations.establishes: The required alternative combined service allocation aligns closely with the stated $1.8 billion figure.

citations.finding: The narrowest reading of roads-only profiles (excluding Neighbourhood Renewal and bridges) totals $1.117 billion, less than the stated $1.8 billion.
citations.establishes: A strict Service Category definition of roads yields a significantly lower figure.

citations.finding: CM-20-0330 was approved at $100 million, allocated as $5.950 million in 2023, $26.750 million in 2024, $33.650 million in 2025 and $33.650 million in 2026.
citations.establishes: The approved numerator, its four-year period and annual allocation; Appendix A page 102 and profile pages 539-542 print amounts in thousands.

citations.finding: The prescribed roads-only profile sum is $1.945703 billion, equal to 19.457 times the $100 million CM-20-0330 allocation.
citations.establishes: The adopted 2023-2026 amounts and service-category labels for every profile in the brief's prescribed primary boundary.

citations.finding: Table 8 reports $622.8 million in growth and $1,171.2 million in renewal for the combined Active Pathways and Roads Service, totalling $1.7940 billion.
citations.establishes: The required combined-service alternative and its full published label; page 55 reports amounts in millions.
citations.quote: Active Pathways and Roads Service: 622.8 growth; 1,171.2 renewal; 1,794.0 total

citations.finding: CM-20-0330's adopted 2023-2026 total is $100 million.
citations.establishes: The denominator used for the roads-to-bike-lane ratios.

citations.finding: The narrowest boundary—profiles carrying only the Roads service-category label—totals $1.116532 billion, or 11.165 times the bike-lane profile.
citations.establishes: A reasonable narrower definition produces an order-of-magnitude advantage for roads but not approximately $1.8 billion under the brief's cutoffs.

citations.finding: The City's only published service-level figure near $1.8 billion is explicitly labelled Active Pathways and Roads Service, not roads alone.
citations.establishes: Calling the $1.7940 billion Table 8 line a roads total would erase the active-pathway component.

citations.finding: The constructed primary total crosses the City's service-level presentation because it includes profiles shown under Traffic Safety and the Yellowhead Trail transformation as well as Roads and Neighbourhood Renewal labels.
citations.establishes: The primary total is reproducible under the brief's boundary but is not a total the City itself prints as a single roads line.

items.title: City of Edmonton, Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Parks & Roads Services program summary, Snow and Ice Control

citations.finding: Approved 2019-2022 Operating Budget, Branch Parks & Roads Services, 'Approved 2019 - 2022 Budget - Program Summary', Program Name Snow and Ice Control, printed page 212 (PDF page 216), Resources ($000): Revenue & Transfers $13 (2022 Budget); Expenditure & Transfers 64,466 (2022 Budget); Subtotal 64,453; Intra-municipal Recoveries (800); Total Net Operating Requirement $63,653; FTE 225.9. The branch summary by program (printed page 205, PDF page 209) shows Snow and Ice Control net expenditure 63,666 for 2022.
citations.establishes: The primary denominator cell as printed: $64,466 thousand; ratio 100,000/64,466 = 1.551.

citations.finding: The 2022 Approved Operating Budget for Snow and Ice Control (Expenditure & Transfers) was $64,466,000.
citations.establishes: The primary denominator for the snow budget comparison.

citations.finding: A budget of $100 million is 1.55 times $64.47 million, not double.
citations.establishes: The arithmetic ratio is roughly half again, rather than double.

citations.finding: The adopted 2022 Snow and Ice Control program summary reports Expenditure & Transfers of $64.466 million and a Total Net Operating Requirement of $63.653 million, with the table printed in thousands.
citations.establishes: The brief's primary 2022 gross denominator and the contextual net denominator, both from the Snow and Ice Control program summary on page 212.
citations.quote: Expenditure & Transfers: 64,466; Total Net Operating Requirement: 63,653

items.title: Global News, 'City council hearing mixed reaction on $100 million to Edmonton bike plan'

citations.finding: Global News, December 12, 2022: 'Ward Papastew Councillor Michael Janz said ... "Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads."'
citations.establishes: The wording of the claim as reported, including the '180 times' figure that does not follow from the two dollar amounts.
citations.quote: Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.

citations.finding: The reported quotation says $1.8 billion is "180 times" $100 million, although the two stated dollar figures imply eighteen times.
citations.establishes: The arithmetic discrepancy in the circulating quotation; it does not establish the budget totals independently.
citations.quote: Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.
